summary.tagline: Mizen Head (Irish: Carn Uí Néid) is traditionally regarded as the most southerly point of mainland Ireland alt

travel.headline: Check visitor access before departure

days.title: Mizen Tip and Harbor Villages
days.start: Suggested: 9 AM start, after checking official access hours

stops.name: Crookhaven
stops.detail: Here lies the small village of Crookhaven with its protected harbor.

stops.name: Mizen Head Visitor Centre
stops.detail: Via a bridge you can reach the lighthouse and the Mizen Head Visitor Centre on the offshore cliff, where the rough surf of the Atlantic creates high spray.

stops.name: Goleen
stops.detail: The village of Goleen was built in the 19th century at a crossroads where cattle shows were held.

days.title: Sailing, Mountains and Ancient Tombs
days.start: Suggested: 9 AM start, after checking official access hours

stops.name: Mount Gabriel
stops.detail: At 407 m high, Mount Gabriel is the largest mountain not only on the Mizen Peninsula, but also in the entire region east and south of Bantry.

stops.name: Schull
stops.detail: Schull is a sailing town that attracts visitors in summer with festivals and regattas and has its season that goes on into the night in Ireland's only planetarium.

stops.name: Wedge Tombs von Toormore und Altar
stops.detail: Near Toormore (Tuar Mór) lie the wedge tombs of Toormore and Altar and the portal tomb of Arderawinny.
